Subject: QuantEdge: request for per-tenant concurrency caps + graceful fallback lane

Team —

Quick heads-up and ask from QuantEdge (high growth quant trading shop). They want a production-safe way to protect against tenant-induced tail spikes while keeping their live LLM features online. Procurement has signaled that this capability is a gating item for the MSA/POC to move to committed deal (deal id QEC-2027-03).

Business ask: implement per-tenant concurrency caps at routing level and a graceful degraded fallback path (automated routing to a smaller, CPU-backed variant when a tenant exceeds their concurrency window) so their SLAs stay within 95th pct latency targets. They want this as a condition for a 12-month Dedicated capacity commitment.

Can Eng/Product estimate:
- short-term mitigation (config + routing rule + capacity reservation) — timeline and risk?
- medium-term product work (native per-tenant concurrency + automated fallback + observability) — rough effort and prioritization impact?

Attached: preliminary SOW and a sample QPS export they sent.

Thanks — Aisha
--

Subject: Re: QuantEdge: request for per-tenant concurrency caps + graceful fallback lane

Thanks for the context, Aisha. I reviewed the sample QPS export (quantedge_qps_sample.csv) — they have a pronounced heavy tail: 99th pct of requests cluster in bursts up to ~15x baseline for short windows.

Feasibility notes:
- Short-term: We can implement a routing-layer mitigation in 3–5 business days: a tenant-specific routing rule that enforces a max concurrent request limit and routes overflow to a fallback model variant hosted on CPU/GPU with lower cost. This would be an operational shim (config only) and require SRE support to add capacity reservation and runbook.
- Medium-term (product): Proper per-tenant concurrency controls + policy UI + auto-fallback needs API, routing policy changes, and bookkeeping for per-tenant counters; ballpark 3–4 engineer-weeks across runtime + routing + console to be safe. Add 1 week for QA and rollout canary.

Trade-offs: the CPU fallback will increase latency and may affect output parity — we should define acceptance criteria (latency thresholds, quality regressions allowed). Also need a plan for token billing alignment when fallback occurs.

Questions for the customer: targeted 95th/99th latency SLO numbers and acceptable quality delta for fallback. Can they commit to a short-term capacity reservation (a 'deal surge lane') to make the config-only approach viable?

I'll be available to scope the routing rule runbook if we lock the mitigation path.

— Dev
Dev Patel

Subject: Re: QuantEdge: request for per-tenant concurrency caps + graceful fallback lane

Looping in engineering perspective. Short answers: doable, but timeline and support model matter.

Option A (fast): routing rule + reserved capacity + manual runbook (SRE) — ~1 week to validate + we need commitment for dedicated nodes during peak windows. Good for Q1 go/no-go.
Option B (product): build native per-tenant concurrency + auto-fallback + visibility in Console — this is higher quality but 3–5 weeks of focused effort (PM + 2 engs + QE). This should be prioritized against current sprint work; it will displace at least one planned infra task.

Operational asks if we go fast: who owns running the surge lane, what escalation keys, and who pays for overage during the trial? If QuantEdge signs a 12-month Dedicated commitment, we can accelerate Option B with a small engineering allocation.

Acceptance criteria request (what Product needs to ship for the customer to sign):
- Configurable concurrency cap per tenant with enforcement in routing.
- Automated fallback to a named model variant with documented quality degradation.
- Console metric: per-tenant concurrency, fallback count, and 95/99 latency charts.
- Runbook for SRE with rollback and alerting thresholds.

I also created a HubSpot deal link for the team to reference: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/1234567/QEC-2027-03

Jonas

Aisha —

Thanks for escalating. We can confirm this is a gating requirement for the pilot -> committed contract. Our procurement timeline is tight: we need to finalize commercial terms by 2027-02-18. Attached LOI and the SOW draft. QuantEdge can commit to a 12-month Dedicated capacity if the fallback and concurrency guarantees are in place and documented.

SLOs we care about: 95th < 250ms for the primary model under normal load; fallback allowed to 95th < 1200ms but should remain available. Quality: we expect fallbacks to maintain answer format and avoid hallucinations beyond a defined set — happy to share evaluation prompts.

Happy to jump on a short call with engineering to clarify scope.

Great thread — thanks everyone. Proposal for next steps so we can move the commercials: 

1) Short-term (target: next 7 business days):
   - Dev + SRE implement routing rule + capacity reservation + fallback to pre-provisioned smaller variant. (Dev to own runbook)
   - Draft acceptance criteria doc capturing latency bands, quality checks, and billing behavior for fallback. (Marissa to own)
   - We offer a 30-day pilot credit and a commitment window for the Dedicated contract contingent on passing acceptance tests.

2) Medium-term (target: 3–5 weeks):
   - Product sprint to build native per-tenant concurrency enforcement + Console visibility. This will be scoped as a high-priority post-pilot task if QuantEdge signs the 12-month commit.

3) Meeting: Schedule a 30-min sync (engineering + QuantEdge) tomorrow morning PT to align on acceptance criteria and runbook. Aisha — can you confirm availability? Dev — please prepare a brief runbook outline and cost estimate for the surge lane.

Attachments: I uploaded the latest SOW and LOI to the deal record (links above).

If we get a yes on the pilot acceptance criteria, we can lock the commercial by 2027-02-18 as requested.
